reviews.text: Great app, some hurdles to use. This is the best bird ID app available for Apple devices. So straightforward to use, and lovingly presented. NOTE: The app will ask you for account login or email address in order to access it, and this cannot be done without cell or WiFi access, and the process for downloading the app's content to your phone so that the app works without connectivity doesn't get pushed through until *after* you log in, so make sure you get everything set up at home before you take it into the field.

comprehensive and user-friendly!. i’ve been using this app for about a week now, and i absolutely adore it! 

- the bird identification feature goes far beyond the scope of other apps ive tried, it’s highly in depth and isnt as restrictive. you can easily narrow down what bird you saw from all the appearance options. i also appreciate the option to choose based on call alone! you’d have to dig for that specific call in some other apps, and having that option makes things much easier! you can’t always see the bird youre hearing.

- i find myself looking at the photography section of the explore page a lot. it’s nice to physically see birds that were spotted instead of looking at locations and data! it feels more real to me that way.

- the custom lists are very handy. you can pick what birds are on them based on their names, but there’s also a box with their appearance! they also have the option to push notifications if theyre spotted within a certain radius. they tell you where the bird was spotted and when! (date and time) 

- with ebird functions built in, it makes it easier to find spots for birding! all it needs is a general location and itll tell you exactly what spots are nearby and how many birds have been spotted there both in total and recently! super convenient for those who don’t want two separate apps just for one function. 

- my only real complaint is i wish there were more birds! there’re so many different species from all across the world, i think it would be nice to see birds from outside north america! it would make the app more accessible to people from different countries too.

overall, i highly recommend this app! the app is very customizable, the id features are precise and accurate, inputting sightings is easy, and each species has a thorough explanation of their behaviors as well as sighting maps! very user friendly as well as informative!

Audubon vs Merlin. So I originally used Merlin and didn’t really know this app existed. However, I have an older phone and was not able to update to IOS 16, so was not able to use Merlin anymore as it requires 16 or above. I found this app which is amazing and is totally free! Also, the Bird ID option is awesome!!! On merlin it’s just a few questions that doesn’t narrow it down much. Just size, color, habitait, and activity. Audubon though has options for those AS WELL AS wing shape, tail shape, and best of all type. It was so annoying with Merlin when I was trying to ID a songbird and the options were raptors. On Audubon those won’t even show up! Audubon also has in my opinion much more information about the individual birds and a better designed app. There are a few things I like about Merlin better though. Merlin obviously connected right to my EBird account which was very useful. It also had bird packs for all over the world, while Audubon only has the US and Canada. Audubon also doesn’t have a sound or photo id, which is annoying. If the developers added this the app would definitely be much better then Merlin. I suggest, if you can, to download both Merlin and Audubon. Merlin for the photo and sound id and EBird, Audubon for everything else. Thank you for reading my review! Good luck birding! 😁🪶
